findings.text: Built in symbol names are stored compressed and expanded on demand into a caller buffer. A length header that may occupy one or two storage units depending on a high bit tells how many compressed units follow. Each compressed unit is translated through an index and a token table and the resulting characters are appended, except that the very first output character is discarded as it encodes the symbol type. Copying respects the caller capacity and terminates the output when room remains, and the helper reports the location of the following symbol in the compressed stream.

Symbol type is derived without full expansion by inspecting only the opening token of the compressed representation and returning its leading character, adjusting the inspected position when the length header signals an extended form.
Address lookup for a core symbol index selects between a directly embedded stored value on narrow non relocatable builds and a decoded relative offset converted to a pointer on other builds.

A core iteration step clears the module label, resolves the address from the current position, resolves the type from the current name offset, expands the name into the iterator name buffer within its capacity, and reports how far the compressed stream advanced.

Extended iteration walks additional symbol sources in a fixed sequence, starting with loadable modules, then tracer module symbols, then packet filter symbols, then probe symbols. Each stage is tried only while its recorded end marker is unset or lies beyond the current position, and the position passed to each stage is relative to the end of the prior stage. A miss records the current position as the end for that stage.

Module symbol lookup treats the requested number as global across all modules. It skips modules that have not completed formation, dereferences per module symbol tables, and subtracts each table size until the owning module is found. On a hit it fills value, type, name, module label and exported flag from module metadata; otherwise it reports out of range.

Export status is decided by binary searching the appropriate sorted export table for the name, using the core table when no module is given and the module table otherwise, then confirming that the stored export address equals the symbol value, decoding relative values where the platform requires it.

Probe symbol lookup threads a remaining index through available slot caches before consulting an architecture hook. Each cache consumes one count per page and the first cache that contains the index supplies the entry; if none matches, an out of range indication is returned. The default architecture hook always reports absence.

Debugger symbol completion keeps a persistent walk position across calls, resetting it when the caller signals a fresh search. It walks successive symbol names and returns the first name that starts with the given prefix, copying it into the caller buffer within its capacity, or reports no match when the walk exhausts.

Debugger output filtering matches a candidate line against a pattern while ignoring a trailing newline. When both anchor flags are set the lengths must match exactly; with only a leading anchor the pattern must appear at the start; with only a trailing anchor at the end; otherwise the pattern may appear anywhere in the line.

Console ownership acquisition first attempts a direct take, then a handover with retry on a transient indication, then a hostile take. Only one path needs to succeed. On success the context selects panic buffers when the current processor is the panicking one and normal buffers otherwise, and loads the record sequence from which printing should resume.

Direct acquisition refuses when a panic is active on another processor unless debugger printing is active locally or the attempt is a reacquire without prior unsafe takeover. It also refuses when the caller priority does not strictly exceed both current and requested priorities, and when the console is marked unsafe. On acceptance it installs a new state carrying caller priority, cleared request, takeover derived unsafe marking, and current processor identity via an atomic compare exchange loop.

Console sequence values are stored in narrow form and expanded to wide form by folding around the oldest available ringbuffer sequence, tolerating a large but bounded lag between console and producer. A trivial identity mapping exists for builds without the expansion helper.

Descriptor and info entries are located by masking a running identifier down to the ring capacity. A packed state value carries an identity portion and a small state portion; a mismatch of the identity portion means the slot has been recycled and is reported as a miss, otherwise the state portion is returned.

Module list traversal for symbol lookup executes under an automatic cleanup based read side guard, using read side list iteration and read side dereference for per module symbol data, so that concurrent module removal is deferred until the lookup completes.
Probe slot cache traversal holds a read side lock across the whole page list walk, releasing it before returning, so page reclamation cannot free a page while it is being inspected.

Debugger message fanout traverses the console collection under a sleepable read lock, sampling each console flags under that lock and releasing the lock after the walk, while legacy writes additionally elevate a global crash recursion indicator around each driver call to discourage internal locking.
Nonblocking console state is observed with an atomic snapshot and mutated only with an atomic compare exchange retry loop, so concurrent ownership attempts serialize without sleeping.

Printk descriptor reads use ordered loads with read barriers between state sampling, content copying, and state re sampling, and the oldest sequence helper loops with a barrier until the tail slot is observed in a stable finalized or reusable condition.

Observed iterator state includes a walk position, a name offset, a resolved value and type, fixed capacity buffers for symbol name and module label, an exported flag, and separate end markers for module, tracer module, and packet filter sources that make exhausted stages sticky.

Observed nonblocking write context includes an output buffer pointer and length, a takeover marker copied from current console state, and an embedded acquisition context holding console reference, priority level, selected print buffers, and starting record sequence.

Observed console ownership state includes current priority, requested priority, unsafe marking, unsafe takeover history, owning processor, and a single atomic word that carries all of those fields for compare exchange.

Observed ringbuffer entry splits stable indexing metadata from record metadata. The descriptor side holds a state variable and a text block locator; the info side holds a wide sequence number and a caller identifier. Both sides share the same masked index derived from the running identifier.

Kallsyms iteration forms a chain with sticky termini. The walker remains in one source until that source reports exhaustion, at which point its end marker is set and later positions skip it permanently for that walk, eventually falling through to probe symbols as the final stage.

Console acquisition forms a fallback chain. A direct attempt that reports contention moves to handover, a handover that reports retry repeats, contention after handover moves to hostile takeover, and any definitive refusal aborts the whole attempt without further stages.

Descriptor slots as observed move between inconsistent and stable observations. Inconsistent observations cause early return with details preserved, while only finalized or reusable observations are accepted as the oldest record; other states cause the oldest sequence helper to reload and retry.

Name expansion may truncate when caller capacity is exhausted. Copying stops early, the output holds a prefix, and termination is written only when room remains, so callers must handle prefix results and must not assume full names.

Debugger console fanout assumes all other processors are stopped and that selected drivers tolerate reentry while a crash indicator is elevated. Drivers that cannot tolerate such reentry may misbehave, and nonblocking consoles that cannot be acquired are silently skipped for that message.

Once an unsafe hostile takeover has occurred, direct acquisition is never considered safe again. The code emits a one time warning if such history is observed on the direct path and propagates the history into the new unsafe marking.

Input draining busy polls all registered poll callbacks with watchdog touches and a brief delay between passes, continuing until a full pass observes no input. A continuously active input source can therefore delay return.

Panic location checks rely on the panicking processor identifier remaining stable and on the current processor identity being sampled without migration, which the code justifies by reasoning that migration relative to the panicking processor cannot occur once that identifier is set.
Synthetic symbol sources use fixed module labels with exported status always cleared, namely bpf for packet filter symbols and __builtin__kprobes for probe symbols.
Probe slot cache entries report a fixed single letter type t, a name taken from the cache template, and an address derived from the page instruction area.
Packed descriptor state encodes identity in the low portion and a small state selector in a shifted flag field, decoded by DESC_ID and DESC_STATE.
Debugger emergency console acquisition uses NBCON_PRIO_EMERGENCY, and successful direct acquisition clears any pending request to NBCON_PRIO_NONE.
Symbol and module labels use fixed capacity buffers governed by KSYM_NAME_LEN and MODULE_NAME_LEN, and helpers never write beyond the supplied capacity.
Core address lookup is provided as a globally visible helper that maps a symbol index to an address, handling both directly stored and relatively encoded offset tables.
Module symbol lookup is provided as a globally visible helper that maps a global symbol number across all modules to value, type, name, module label and exported status.
Probe symbol lookup is provided as a globally visible family covering aggregate dispatch, per cache page selection, and a weak architecture fallback that always reports absence.
Printk helpers are provided as globally visible operations for oldest sequence retrieval, console sequence expansion, and write context buffer attachment.

Panic location queries are provided as globally visible predicates for whether the current processor is the panicking one, whether a panic is in progress elsewhere, and whether any panic is in progress.
Extended kallsyms dispatch acts as the entry that selects among module, tracer module, packet filter and probe sources for positions beyond the core symbol count.
Debugger input drain, line matching, message fanout and prefix completion act as debugger entries for interactive symbol work and output handling.
Emergency console acquisition for the debugger acts as the entry that builds a zeroed acquisition context at emergency priority and attempts ownership plus unsafe entry.
